maps.name: Using a community noticeboard
maps.context: A resident uses a physical noticeboard at a neighbourhood centre to find a local event and leave information for other people.
maps.notes: Observed mappings describe a short walkthrough using a paper prototype. Conceptualised mappings suggest aspects that could be explored through rearranging the board and observing how people interact with it.

rows.description: Observed: The large framed board, visible papers, and open push-pin area suggest that people can read, add, and rearrange notices.
signifiers: Push-pins stored in a small tray

rows.description: Observed: Coloured headings make the categories visible from a short distance, but the meaning of each colour is not immediately clear to a new visitor.
rows.change: Pair each colour with a plain-language category label and a simple symbol.

rows.description: Conceptualised: A small set of available pins and a limited writing area could guide people toward shorter, more readable notices.
rows.change: Test a notice template with a clear title, date, location, and contact area.

rows.description: Conceptualised: A dated notice and a marked review area could communicate how a person should remove or update information without needing staff assistance.
rows.change: Prototype a visible review date and a dedicated area for notices awaiting removal.

rows.description: Conceptualised: If every notice uses the same title position, date format, and category mark, people can scan the board more easily.
rows.change: Create three notice templates and compare how quickly people find relevant information.
